Subject: EdgeFin benchmark methodology & performance SLO follow-up

Hi Jamie / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off a formal benchmark: 

Summary of targets you confirmed:
- Latency: p50 ~ 30-50ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 < 200ms (for the 2k token generation profile)
- Throughput: sustained 500 req/s for typical prompt mix; burst to 1k req/s for short periods
- Concurrency: expected up to 50 concurrent sessions; ability to route degraded requests to lower-cost variants
- Streaming: partial token flushes required at ~100ms granularity for UI responsiveness; also need server-side SSE support

We'd like to validate these with a reproducible benchmark. To keep this efficient, our suggested methodology: 
1) You share a canonical prompt set + workload profile (request mix, token lengths, streaming vs non-streaming) — ideally in CSV/JSON.
2) We run a baseline on Redwood hosted using your prompt set and our internal harness (will provide scripts), collect p50/p95/p99 latencies, tail latencies, throughput, GPU utilization, and streaming flush latencies.
3) We'll provide an artifact with raw logs, measurement definitions, and reproducible run steps.

Can you send the prompt set and any evaluation harness constraints (e.g., auth, arrival patterns)?

Proposed next steps: 
- Jamie: share prompt set + expected request mix by EOD Tuesday (Jul 21)
- Marissa / Redwood infra: schedule benchmark run & share methodology doc
- Technical sync if needed after initial run to refine metrics/quantization tradeoffs

Attaching a sample template for prompt metadata (see attachment: edgefin_prompt_set_v2.csv).

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming we can share the prompt set and workload profile. Attached is the prompt CSV and a lightweight workload descriptor (edgefin_workload_profile.json). A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- The p99 target is tight for our longer flows (up to ~2k tokens). If model quantization or smaller variants cause regressions in generation quality, we'd prefer fallback rules vs returning errors.
- Streaming: our front-end expects a partial chunk every ~100-150ms for progressive rendering. If you can measure the streaming flush latency distribution that would be ideal.
- Reproducibility: we run our own harness in CI; would like the Redwood run to output the raw latency traces and the command-line runbook so we can reproduce locally.

Attaching: edgefin_prompt_set_v2.csv, edgefin_workload_profile.json. We can also provide a Dockerized harness if useful (we'll upload to the shared Drive).

Marissa / team —

Quick read of the prompt set and workload profile. Initial notes and a proposed measurement plan below.

Proposed infra for a representative run:
- Dedicated Redwood pod: 4x A100 80GB (to keep memory headroom for 2k tokens)
- Client driver nodes: 4 x c6i.8xlarge-ish instances to generate arrival patterns and sustained throughput

Measurement definitions / plan:
- Request-level latency: measure from request submission to first-byte and to final-byte (useful for streaming vs full responses). Report p50/p95/p99 for both first-byte and final-byte.
- Token-flush latency: instrument server to emit timestamps per flush boundary; compute flush-latency distribution and p50/p95/p99 of flush intervals.
- Throughput: measure sustained RPS over 5-minute windows and peak sustained 1-minute windows.
- Resource metrics: per-GPU GPU utilization, memory, NVLink, CPU usage on driver nodes.
- Reproducibility: package the harness run as a Docker image + runbook with exact client seed, request schedule, and model artifact SHA. Include raw logs (ndjson) + aggregated CSVs.

Caveats / tradeoffs:
- Quantization can reduce latency by ~20-40% depending on model family but may cause small quality regressions; plan to run A/B on a 5k sample to measure ROUGE/semantic-similarity metrics.
- Streaming depends on internal batching; to achieve 100-150ms flushes we may need to tune batching windows which could impact throughput. We'll document batching config and its effect.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Run a quick smoke with hosted infra to validate the harness and capture base numbers (1h).
2) If numbers look promising, run the full dedicated run with raw logs & reproducible artifacts.

I'll draft a minimal runbook and share the Drive link by EOD.

- Aditya
